description: Recall eval for the 0Latency memory product. Each question is asked against the live /recall endpoint; an LLM judge scores the returned context_block against an expected-facts rubric. Questions marked answer_changed_over_time have a stale prior answer still present in the store, so passing requires recall to surface the CURRENT answer and not present the superseded one as current.

questions.question: What is the current state of the 0latency API key — is it usable?
questions.conversation_context: Checking whether the 0latency API key currently works before making API calls.
expected_facts: The 0latency API key is currently invalid or expired
The user does have / did have a key in the zl_live_ format
must_not_assert: That the API key is currently valid and working, stated without any mention that it is invalid or expired
questions.notes: The canonical F3 silent-supersession pair: 340de444 (has key) and b2b76357 (key invalid/expired), both live, both typed fact, neither carrying contradicts. Recall must surface the later state. This question is the direct user-visible cost of the F3 gap.

questions.question: Which git branch is the Chrome extension work currently on?
questions.conversation_context: Resuming work on the 0Latency Chrome extension repo and need the current working branch.
expected_facts: The current chrome-extension branch is fix/dup-turns-auth-gate
must_not_assert: That the current extension working branch is master or main
questions.notes: Branch changed 2026-08-21. The workspace clone on the box is still on master with a single initial commit, so a wrong answer here is plausible-looking.

questions.question: Is Chrome extension memory capture actually working, or is it broken when the extension reports 0 memories stored?
questions.conversation_context: The extension shows memories_stored: 0 on many turns and we need to know whether capture is failing.
expected_facts: Capture is working / not broken
memories_stored counts only newly-extracted salient atoms, not the raw turn
The verbatim raw turn is stored every turn regardless, so 0 does not mean nothing was captured
must_not_assert: That Chrome extension capture is failing or dropping turns when it reports 0
questions.notes: Answer inverted at the CP-INJECT P3-A1 diagnostic (2026-06-26): the earlier read was 'capture failure', the verified answer is 'observability/interpretation issue'.

questions.question: What is the defensible LongMemEval benchmark number for 0Latency, and how must it be reported?
questions.conversation_context: Preparing an investor-facing comparison against Mem0 and need the number we can actually defend.
expected_facts: The banked/defensible result is 76% at Recall@20
Reported together with MRR 0.5366 and precision 0.9851
A lone ceiling number is not defensible; the full metric set must be reported
must_not_assert: That 88% is the achieved defensible benchmark number
That 40% is the current result without noting it was not comparable
questions.notes: The store holds three competing live numbers: 76%@20 (banked, correct), 88% (an aspirational target that leaked into a headline as if achieved), and a 40% run explicitly recorded as not comparable. This question tests whether recall resolves the conflict or just returns the loudest row.

questions.question: Why was the embedding-similarity fallback for finding a supersession target removed?
questions.conversation_context: Considering adding a similarity fallback when the extraction LLM gives no contradicts_id.
expected_facts: It produced a large number of wrong supersessions (roughly 500+ per benchmark run)
Corrections vague-matched onto unrelated memories
It was removed deliberately; precision is the binding constraint
questions.notes: Stable design constraint. Guards against a future chain reintroducing the trap.

questions.question: How does a correction memory supersede an older memory — what has to be present for it to fire?
questions.conversation_context: Debugging why some corrections never superseded anything.
expected_facts: The memory must be typed as a correction
It must carry a contradicts_id naming the target memory
The target must still exist and be unsuperseded
questions.notes: Tests recall of the three-gate mechanism documented in the contradiction-detection design.

questions.question: Does the recall candidate pool include raw_turn rows?
questions.conversation_context: Investigating why a verbatim conversation turn appeared in recall results.
expected_facts: The vector path excludes raw_turn rows (extracted atoms only)
The BM25 keyword fast-path does not filter raw_turn, so keyword-dominant queries can surface them
must_not_assert: That raw_turn rows are excluded from every recall path with no exception
questions.notes: CP-INJECT P3-B1 finding. A split answer — a judge should not accept only half.

questions.question: Where does the memory product run and how is it reached?
questions.conversation_context: Need to connect to the memory service to run a diagnostic.
expected_facts: It runs on the box at 164.90.156.169
Reached over SSH as root
questions.notes: Basic environment recall. Scoped to agent thomas: the host fact is held under thomas, not user-justin. Exercises the per-question agent_id override.

questions.question: What is the hard spending control on benchmark runs and why does it exist?
questions.conversation_context: About to launch a LongMemEval run.
expected_facts: --max-cost 3 is mandatory on the runner invocation
It exists because of a prior unbraked-spend incident (roughly $400+ against a configured limit)
questions.notes: Tests recall of a hard operational constraint with a stated cause.

questions.question: Where are the Project Explore Season 2 scripts stored?
questions.conversation_context: Looking for the Season 2 script files for Project Explore.
expected_facts: In the clawd-workspace layla-friends season2 area
questions.notes: Non-engineering domain fact — checks the store is not only good at recalling its own build history.
